correctness.rationale: The bounded census was independently reconstructed. The inequality h<=14 gives max(|p|,|q|)<=floor(e^14)=1,202,604. Generating all {2,3,5,7,50021}-smooth positive integers up to that bound gives exactly 1,349 values. Exhaustive primitive triples 0<a<=b<c<=1,202,604 with a+b=c give exactly 66 triples, with (1,1,2) the unique symmetric case, so the ordered count is 6*66-3=393. Exactly three triples use 50021: (1,300125,300126), (21,50000,50021), and (400,50021,50421). Thus the record correctly refutes the conjunction '212 symmetry classes and all solutions of height <=14'.

originality.rationale: The public von Känel–Matschke data page tabulates the first-n-prime sets and all sets with prime-product/radical coverage through 10^7; {2,3,5,7,50021} has product 10,504,410 and is not one of those tabulated sets. Searches for the exact prime set and the integers 66/393 did not locate a prior census. The three 50021-containing triples are therefore genuinely new bounded computational data relative to the cited public tables, even though the enumeration method itself is routine.

scientific_value.rationale: The result is too narrow to validate as a standalone research finding. The cutoff h<=14 is inherited from the target being refuted, not from an intrinsic arithmetic threshold, and the audit leaves the actual unbounded S-unit equation for this S completely open. Relative to the public tables, the new mathematical content is a finite box search producing three additional large-prime triples plus inherited {2,3,5,7} solutions. This is useful regression/test data, but it does not establish a new Diophantine theorem, height bound, or complete census.
